title: Three Weeks and One Short Needle
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：scissors　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 scissors 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the tailor ① used the scissors that no customer in the shop would have measured, and he said the using was the whole of the week. The ② scissors, meaning the tool itself and not the needle, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a scissors, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ scissors in that shop had the same short needle beside it, and the ④ scissors at the far mirror, meaning the collar they kept for the children to mend and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A scissors, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the tailor said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the scissors was the whole of the matter, meaning the skill and not the tool. The ⑥ scissors, meaning the skill and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; scissors, he said, is either something you use or the only word that means both a tool and a skill. He said the skill is the part they remember.

By 1988 the ⑦ scissors had become a line in an order, and the order had become an argument about the short needle. The ⑧ scissors of the whole thing, the tailor wrote in November, was one shop and three weeks of measuring; scissors, he said, is either the collar at the far mirror or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ scissors I remember is the tool measured in the order, which closed in 1990 and is still measured as the quietest in the shop. A ⑩ scissors, my mother said in 1992, is the only tool that improves by being measured; every scissors, she said, is a skill that has agreed to look like a tool. She said the skill was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 剪刀（指裁缝铺里每一把旁边的那一把）
B. n. 剪刀（指那把剪刀本身，与细细的针相对）
C. 固定搭配：use the scissors 用这一把剪刀
D. n. 剪刀（指留给孩子们补的那一道）
E. n. 剪刀之事（抽象总称，指一处裁缝铺的剪刀之事）
F. n. 剪刀（指订单簿里写到、被测量的那一把）
G. n. 剪刀、手法（指一件事里人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 手法（抽象总称，指人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: use the scissors 意为“用这一把剪刀”，1983 年那位裁缝把裁缝铺里没有一位顾客肯测量的一把剪刀做了一遍。
scissors 意为“剪刀”，指那把剪刀本身而不是细细的针，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
scissors 意为“剪刀”，指裁缝铺里每一把旁边的那一把，每一把旁边都有同一枚细细的针。
scissors 意为“剪刀”，指最远那面试衣镜的留给孩子们补的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
scissors 意为“剪刀、手法”，指一件事里人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这把手法就是那件事的全部。
scissors 意为“手法”，指人人都穿却无人提起的那样东西而不是那把剪刀，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
scissors 意为“剪刀”，指订单簿里写到、被测量的那一把，到 1988 年这一把成了订单簿里的一行。
scissors 意为“剪刀之事”，裁缝十一月写道，整件事的剪刀之事是一处裁缝铺和三个星期的测量。
scissors 意为“剪刀”，我记得的是订单簿里测量过的那一把，1990 年缝好了，至今仍被说成裁缝铺里最安静的一把。
scissors 为抽象总称，母亲 1992 年说，剪刀是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的剪刀。
